title: GDScript LSP initialize synchronously parses every workspace script, causing multi-second handshakes in large projects
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] (latest stable as of 2026-08-30).
- Also reproducible in Godot 4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4].

### System information

Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, build 26200 - x86_64

### Issue description

The first GDScript LSP `initialize` request synchronously scans and parses every `.gd` file under `res://` before returning the initialize response.

On large GDScript workspaces this makes the LSP handshake scale directly with workspace source volume and blocks the client for multiple seconds even though the editor and LSP TCP server are already running.

This is separate from editor startup time: the benchmark starts its timer only after the LSP port accepts the measurement connection, immediately before sending `initialize`, and stops it when the matching response arrives.

Godot 4.7.2 source still has this path in `GDScriptWorkspace::initialize()`:

`initialize()` -> `reload_all_workspace_scripts()` -> recursively list `.gd` files under `res://` -> `get_parse_result(path)` for each file.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/modules/gdscript/language_server/gdscript_workspace.cpp
### Measurements

Synthetic MRP: ordinary non-`class_name` GDScript files, 196 lines per file, each containing typed variables and 32 small typed functions.

Godot 4.7.2 stable:

| Scripts | GDScript lines | `initialize` time |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 0 | 0.294 s |
| 250 | 49,000 | 2.194 s |
| 500 | 98,000 | 3.962 s |
| 1,000 | 196,000 | 5.573 s |

The same 196k-line project was started again with its existing `.godot` cache and the initialize request still took 11.034 s in that run, so the project cache does not eliminate the synchronous workspace work.

For comparison, Godot 4.6.3 stable measured 2.120 s / 3.954 s / 7.621 s for the same 49k / 98k / 196k fixtures.

Expected behavior: LSP initialization should not synchronously block on a full parse/analyze pass over every workspace script. Reusing editor analysis/cache, making indexing incremental/background, or otherwise returning `initialize` before the full workspace scan would avoid multi-second handshakes on large projects.

Related but distinct: #114685 shows the same `initialize -> reload_all_workspace_scripts` path in a crash report. #123007 is about cancellation/responsiveness of long requests after initialization; this report is specifically about the synchronous full-workspace work performed by `initialize` itself.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Generate the synthetic project below.
2. Start Godot 4.7.2 editor with an explicit LSP port, for example `--editor --path <project> --lsp-port 6700`.
3. Wait until the LSP TCP port accepts connections.
4. Connect an LSP client and start a timer immediately before sending `initialize`.
5. Stop the timer when the response with the matching request id is received.
6. Repeat with different `COUNT` values.
### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The following generator creates the entire MRP; no project-specific files are required:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import shutil

COUNT = 1000
root = Path("lsp_initialize_mrp")
scripts = root / "scripts"
scripts.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(root / "project.godot").write_text(
    'config_version=5\n\n[application]\nconfig/name="LSP initialize MRP"\n',
    encoding="utf-8",
)
for path in scripts.rglob("*.gd"):
    path.unlink()
for i in range(COUNT):
    folder = scripts / f"group_{i // 50:03d}"
    folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    lines = ["extends RefCounted", "", f"var seed: int = {i}", ""]
    for j in range(32):
        lines += [f"func f_{j:02d}(x: int) -> int:", f"\tvar y: int = x + seed + {j}", "\tif y % 2 == 0:", "\t\ty += 1", "\treturn y", ""]
    (folder / f"bench_{i:04d}.gd").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
shutil.rmtree(root / ".godot", ignore_errors=True)
print(root.resolve())
```
Measurement client used after the port is listening:

```python
import json, socket, time
from pathlib import Path

root = Path("lsp_initialize_mrp").resolve()
s = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", 6700), timeout=5)
s.settimeout(120)
payload = {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"processId":None,"rootPath":str(root),"rootUri":root.as_uri(),"capabilities":{}}}
raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
started = time.perf_counter()
s.sendall(f"Content-Length: {len(raw)}\r\n\r\n".encode() + raw)
data = b""
while b"\r\n\r\n" not in data:
    data += s.recv(4096)
header, body = data.split(b"\r\n\r\n", 1)
length = next(int(x.split(b":", 1)[1]) for x in header.split(b"\r\n") if x.lower().startswith(b"content-length:"))
while len(body) < length:
    body += s.recv(65536)
response = json.loads(body[:length])
print(f"initialize: {time.perf_counter() - started:.3f}s", response.get("error"))
s.close()
```

Changing `COUNT` to 250 and 500 gives the smaller benchmark points above.
